plan.angle:
LANE A (search question); log 'lane: A' in metadata. Series: 'Is a GLP-1 Right for You?'. Build every line from Medicare.gov fact sheet 12234, CMS pages and the official drug labels, each credited and dated with day, month and year. The local TV coverage (WCPO, 22 Oct 2026) may appear only as a one-line hook.

0–15 s: say what viewers will know by the end (who qualifies, which medicines are covered, what you pay, what counts toward the Part D cap, and what to ask your plan). Then give the first concrete answer: the eligibility rule in the fact sheet's own words.

Chapters, named as searched questions:
(1) What is the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
(2) Who qualifies? Copy the four requirements word for word.
(3) Which medicines are covered? Use the fact sheet's exact product list (the radar says Wegovy injection and tablets, Zepbound KwikPen and Foundayo; confirm each). Generic name first, brand in brackets, and say what each one is FDA-approved for.
(4) How long does it run? 1 Jul 2026 to 31 Dec 2027.
(5) Does the $50 count toward the Part D out-of-pocket cap? Confirm the $2,100 figure and the counting rule from Medicare.gov before using either.
(6) What does open enrollment change for 2027?
(7) What it doesn't cover. Never use compounded, online or no-prescription sources, and say that Medicare and CMS don't call or text asking for card numbers, if a CMS page says so.
(8) Questions to ask your prescriber and your plan.

Re-hook every 45–75 s. One brief line on the common GI side effects (nausea, diarrhoea, constipation). Never give switching advice: 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own.' The subscribe ask comes after the eligibility payoff. End by naming one already-published long-form in the same playlist, then the full prescriber line. US-only label on screen. No dosing. 8–12 min. Publish at 14:00 ET.

package.description:
Medicare GLP-1 $50 a month: who qualifies and what's covered.
Watch next: How Long Does Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Take to Work?

Quick answer (US only): From July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027, the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge offers eligible Part D enrollees specific GLP-1 weight-management medicines for $50 a month.
You need drug coverage, a prescription for a listed medicine, and to meet the clinical criteria. Ozempic and Mounjaro aren't listed.
Per CMS, the $50 doesn't count toward your Part D deductible or the 2026 $2,100 cap. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea and constipation.

General information, not personal advice. Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
https://www.medicare.gov/publications/12234-medicare-glp-1-bridge-glp-1-drugs-for-50-a-month.pdf
https://www.amcp.org/regulatory-newsbreak-cms-releases-frequently-asked-questions-medicare-glp-1-bridge

scenes.section: What Is the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: So why did Medicare need a bridge at all? It starts with one line of federal law.

scenes.section: What Is the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: The law lets Medicare drug plans leave out certain kinds of drugs. One item on that list, word for word: agents when used for anorexia, weight loss, or weight gain.

visual.quote: Agents when used for anorexia, weight loss, or weight gain.
visual.attribution: Social Security Act §1927(d)(2)(A), applied to Part D by §1860D-2(e)
visual.stock_query: old law book with highlighted line

scenes.retention_device: Micro-story: a decades-old rule behind today's confusion

scenes.section: What Is the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: Notice the words 'when used for'. The rule targets the reason, not the molecule. So semaglutide and tirzepatide could be covered for type 2 diabetes, but not when prescribed for weight loss.

scenes.section: What Is the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: If that ever felt unfair or confusing, you weren't imagining it. Same medicine, different reason, different answer at the counter.

visual.stock_query: frustrated senior shrugging kindly at counter

scenes.section: What Is the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: That's the gap the Bridge crosses. The Medicare.gov fact sheet describes a time-limited program giving eligible Part D enrollees specific GLP-1 medicines for weight management at a fifty-dollar monthly copay.
scenes.retention_device: Payoff of 'why a bridge' plus vivid metaphor

scenes.section: What Is the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: Imagine Linda, sixty-seven, a retired librarian. She has Medicare drug coverage and blood pressure that stays high despite her medicines. Does she qualify?
scenes.retention_device: Relatable hypothetical thread + direct question before chapter change

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: Let's answer Linda. The fact sheet's rules aren't a menu where you pick one. You need to meet all of them.
scenes.retention_device: Chapter card answering the open question

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: First: Medicare drug coverage. Medicare.gov explains you can get it through a stand-alone Part D plan or a Medicare Advantage plan that includes drug coverage. The Bridge itself is run by Medicare, outside your plan.

visual.stock_query: two Medicare plan cards side by side

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: Second: a prescription from your prescriber for one of the covered medicines. No prescription, no Bridge.

visual.stock_query: doctor handing prescription to smiling senior

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: Third: clinical criteria. This is where body mass index, or BMI, comes in, together with specific health conditions.

visual.stock_query: friendly clinic scale and heart icon

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: In broad terms, there are three groups. A BMI of twenty-seven or more with prediabetes, or a past heart attack, stroke or peripheral artery disease. A BMI of thirty or more with certain heart failure, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or certain chronic kidney disease. Or a BMI of thirty-five or more.

items: BMI 27+ with prediabetes, past heart attack, stroke or peripheral artery disease (summary)
BMI 30+ with certain heart failure, uncontrolled high blood pressure or certain chronic kidney disease (summary)
visual.stock_query: three labelled doors to a bridge

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: If you're already taking one of the listed medicines for weight, there may be a path for you too, based on your BMI when you started. Ask your prescriber.
scenes.on_screen_text: Already on one? Ask about your starting BMI
scenes.retention_device: Relief beat for viewers already on treatment

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: People already getting a GLP-1 through Part D for type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea or MASH aren't part of the Bridge.
scenes.on_screen_text: Already on Part D GLP-1? Not Bridge

visual.myth: Everyone on a GLP-1 can switch to the $50 Bridge
visual.fact: Already getting a GLP-1 through Part D for type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea or MASH? Not part of the Bridge (summary)

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: That's our plain-English summary. Your prescriber confirms the exact criteria with Medicare, so go through the fact sheet together.

visual.stock_query: senior and doctor reading fact sheet

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: So, Linda: uncontrolled high blood pressure is on the list. If her BMI is thirty or more and her prescriber confirms she meets the criteria, she may qualify.

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: If you've been told for years that weight is just about trying harder, seeing Medicare help pay for treatment can feel like finally being taken seriously.

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: If this helped, subscribe. Our series 'Is a GLP-1 Right for You?' decodes every new coverage rule and trial result in plain English.

visual.stock_query: Medi mascot pointing at subscribe bell

scenes.retention_device: Single subscribe ask after the eligibility payoff, tied to the series

scenes.section: Who Qualifies for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
scenes.narration: Now, which medicines? Because this is where most people get tripped up, and the list is shorter than you'd think.

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: The fact sheet names specific products, not every GLP-1 medicine on the market.

visual.stock_query: pharmacy shelf with four highlighted boxes

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: Semaglutide injection and semaglutide tablets, both sold as Wegovy. Tirzepatide, as the Zepbound KwikPen. And orforglipron, sold as Foundayo.

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: The FDA approved Wegovy injection on the fourth of June, twenty twenty-one, for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or with overweight plus at least one weight-related condition.

visual.stock_query: labelled Wegovy pen with FDA stamp

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: On the eighth of March, twenty twenty-four, the FDA added a use: reducing the risk of cardiovascular death, heart attack and stroke in adults with established cardiovascular disease and either obesity or overweight.

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: The Wegovy tablet has the same active ingredient, semaglutide, taken as a once-daily pill instead of a weekly injection.

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: The FDA approved Zepbound, which is tirzepatide, on the eighth of November, twenty twenty-three, for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition.

visual.stock_query: labelled Zepbound KwikPen with FDA stamp

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: Then on the twentieth of December, twenty twenty-four, it became the first medicine approved for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity.

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: Foundayo is orforglipron, a once-daily GLP-1 pill from Lilly, listed on the fact sheet for weight management.

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: Here's the catch most people miss: Ozempic and Mounjaro aren't on this list. Those are the diabetes brands, and Medicare drug plans could already cover them for type 2 diabetes.

visual.myth: Ozempic and Mounjaro get the $50 Bridge copay
visual.fact: They're not on the fact sheet's Bridge list

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: If you take one of those for diabetes, nothing here is a reason to change. Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own.

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: One honest note. For semaglutide and tirzepatide, the FDA lists common side effects including nausea, diarrhea and constipation. Your prescriber can help you plan for them.

scenes.section: Which GLP-1 Medicines Are Covered?
scenes.narration: But the date that matters most isn't when the Bridge started. It's when it ends.

scenes.section: How Long Does the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Run?
scenes.narration: According to the fact sheet, the Bridge runs from the first of July, twenty twenty-six, through the thirty-first of December, twenty twenty-seven. That's eighteen months.
scenes.retention_device: Chapter card with the searched answer

scenes.section: How Long Does the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Run?
scenes.narration: At fifty dollars a month, that's nine hundred dollars in Bridge copays across the whole program, for someone eligible from day one.

scenes.section: How Long Does the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Run?
scenes.narration: For Linda, if she qualified and started in November, that's fourteen months of a predictable cost. On a fixed income, predictable matters as much as cheap.

scenes.section: How Long Does the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Run?
scenes.narration: But eighteen months isn't forever. Hold onto that, because it's tied to the question almost nobody asks.

scenes.section: Does the $50 Count Toward the Part D Cap?
scenes.narration: Now the money question people are typing into search bars: does the fifty dollars count toward the Part D out-of-pocket cap?
scenes.retention_device: Chapter named as the searched question

scenes.section: Does the $50 Count Toward the Part D Cap?
scenes.narration: First, the cap itself. Medicare.gov says that in twenty twenty-six, once your out-of-pocket costs for covered Part D drugs reach two thousand one hundred dollars, you won't pay anything more for covered drugs for the rest of the year.

visual.stat_label: 2026 Part D out-of-pocket cap, covered drugs

scenes.section: Does the $50 Count Toward the Part D Cap?
scenes.narration: Put the Bridge next to it. July to December at fifty dollars a month is three hundred dollars, and that three hundred dollars sits outside the cap.

visual.stat_label: Bridge copays, Jul to Dec 2026 (not counted toward the cap)
visual.stock_query: small coin stack outside fenced area

scenes.retention_device: Simple comparison that sets up the answer

scenes.section: Does the $50 Count Toward the Part D Cap?
scenes.narration: Here's the answer: according to CMS, the fifty-dollar Bridge copay does not count toward your Part D deductible or that yearly cap. So if you take other costly medicines, those drugs have to reach the cap on their own.

visual.myth: My $50 Bridge copays help me reach the Part D cap

scenes.section: Does the $50 Count Toward the Part D Cap?
scenes.narration: So budget for the Bridge copay separately from your other Part D costs.

visual.stock_query: senior calmly sorting two budget envelopes

scenes.section: Does the $50 Count Toward the Part D Cap?
scenes.narration: And one misunderstanding to clear up: the fifty-dollar copay is for the listed GLP-1 medicines only, not everything else in your medicine cabinet.

visual.fact: $50 applies to the listed GLP-1 medicines only
visual.stock_query: medicine cabinet with one highlighted box

scenes.section: Does the $50 Count Toward the Part D Cap?
scenes.narration: Which brings us to the calendar on your fridge. Right now, you're inside Medicare's main yearly window for changing health and drug plans.

scenes.section: What Does Open Enrollment Change for 2027?
scenes.narration: Medicare open enrollment runs from the fifteenth of October to the seventh of December, twenty twenty-six. Changes you make start on the first of January, twenty twenty-seven.

scenes.section: What Does Open Enrollment Change for 2027?
scenes.narration: Plans can change their costs, drug lists and pharmacies from year to year, so this year's best fit may not be next year's.

scenes.section: What Does Open Enrollment Change for 2027?
scenes.narration: Medicare's Plan Finder lets you enter your own medicines and pharmacy, then compare twenty twenty-seven plans side by side.

scenes.section: What Does Open Enrollment Change for 2027?
scenes.narration: The Bridge runs outside your Part D plan, but you need Medicare drug coverage to use it. So make sure any plan you pick for twenty twenty-seven still gives you that.

visual.stock_query: senior checking plan card with smile

scenes.section: What Does Open Enrollment Change for 2027?
scenes.narration: Remember, this is about choosing a plan, not choosing a medicine.

scenes.section: What Does Open Enrollment Change for 2027?
scenes.narration: Picture Linda at her kitchen table, Plan Finder open, tea going cold. That's not stress; that's her taking control. But before she clicks enroll, there's one more thing to protect herself from.

visual.stock_query: determined senior at kitchen table laptop

scenes.retention_device: Emotional beat + cliffhanger into scams chapter

scenes.section: What Doesn't the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Cover?
scenes.narration: The Bridge covers the specific FDA-approved products on the fact sheet's list. Compounded versions of semaglutide or tirzepatide aren't on it.

visual.stock_query: approved boxes inside a fenced area

scenes.section: What Doesn't the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Cover?
scenes.narration: The FDA says compounded drugs aren't FDA-approved, which means the agency doesn't review them for safety, effectiveness or quality before they reach patients.

visual.stock_query: FDA inspector with question mark vial

scenes.section: What Doesn't the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Cover?
scenes.narration: So a fifty-dollar headline is never a reason to buy GLP-1s online without a prescription or from so-called research websites. Stick to a licensed pharmacy and a real prescription.

scenes.section: What Doesn't the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Cover?
scenes.narration: Scammers count on confusion. Medicare.gov warns that Medicare, or anyone representing Medicare, won't call you uninvited asking for your Medicare number or other personal information.

scenes.section: What Doesn't the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Cover?
scenes.narration: If a caller promises fifty-dollar GLP-1s in exchange for your Medicare number, hang up. You can report it by calling one eight hundred Medicare.

visual.stock_query: senior hanging up phone with confidence

scenes.section: What Doesn't the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Cover?
scenes.narration: Your route to the Bridge goes through your prescriber, Medicare and your pharmacy, not a stranger on the phone.

scenes.narration: Why can that matter more than the fifty dollars? Because of what research shows happens when people stop these medicines.

scenes.section: What to Ask Your Prescriber, Pharmacy and Medicare
scenes.narration: In the STEP 1 trial extension, adults with obesity or overweight and no diabetes were followed for a year after their weekly semaglutide and lifestyle program ended. On average, the semaglutide group regained about two-thirds of the weight they had lost.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate and safe to ship once the three small fixes below are made. I checked the core Bridge facts against CMS's FAQ (as summarised by AMCP) and NCOA's Bridge guide, and they match:
- **Dates and price:** Jul 1, 2026 to Dec 31, 2027, $50 a month.
- **Covered products:** Wegovy injection and tablets, the Zepbound KwikPen only, and Foundayo. Ozempic and Mounjaro are not listed.
- **Eligibility groups:** BMI 27+ with prediabetes, past heart attack, stroke or peripheral artery disease; BMI 30+ with heart failure, uncontrolled high blood pressure or kidney disease; or BMI 35+.
- **Exclusion:** people already getting a GLP-1 through Part D for diabetes, sleep apnea or fatty liver disease are not part of the Bridge.
- **Cost rules:** the $50 does not count toward the Part D deductible or yearly cap, and Extra Help doesn't reduce it.
- **How it runs:** outside the Part D benefit, through a central processor, with prior authorization from the prescriber.

These match what I know, but I did not fetch the pages this time: the Part D cap ($2,100 in 2026), open enrollment (Oct 15 to Dec 7), the FDA approval dates (Jun 4, 2021; Mar 8, 2024; Nov 8, 2023; Dec 20, 2024) and their wording, the quoted line of federal law, and the STEP 1 extension result (about two-thirds regained, with the authors' 'chronic condition' conclusion).
